report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference: Model B (B − A positive) has a stronger residual-stream signal that points toward culinary / food / restaurant / cooking / baking / food-blog vocabulary and continuations. In other words, B is biased toward “food/restaurant/recipe/blog” style continuations relative to A.

Why I believe this
- The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells repeatedly include restaurant/food vocabulary across many late layers and early token positions: e.g. "restaurant", "Restaurant", "cooking", "Cooking", "Chef", "Chef", "baking", "Cake", "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "Cafe", "kitchen", "cooked", "Cooking", "baker", etc. These tokens appear across layers ~16–25 and across pos0–pos4 in the top differences.
- The L2-norm map shows the difference concentrated in later layers (big peaks at layers 24–25, and large values from ~16 onward) and strongly at the first few token positions (pos0 and pos1 especially). That pattern is consistent with a change that affects top-level semantic/content preferences for continuations (later layers / early-position residuals matter for next-token logits).
- The token pattern is coherent (many culinary / restaurant / blogger/“professional” food-industry tokens), not random, so it reads as a domain/style bias rather than random noise.

Caveats / what I cannot say
- I cannot identify the precise cause (e.g., whether B was fine-tuned on food blogs, had adjusted decoding priors, or some other intervention).
- I cannot attribute it to a named objective beyond “stronger tendency toward culinary/restaurant/food-blog continuations.”
- Patchscope results were not shown in the evidence block, so I relied on the logit-lens + norm distribution.

If you want, I can: (a) try targeted patchscope probes (identity prompts that reveal continuations) to demonstrate the continuation differences concretely, or (b) extract which specific neurons/canonical directions carry the strongest culinary signal.
